title: Nyingma
hookLine: the "ancient" school tracing back to Padmasambhava

lines: A FIGURE ON A LOTUS, A FEATHERED HAT.
cards: A figure sits on a lotus in paintings on temple walls across the Himalayas. He wears a red hat with a feather on top, a curling mustache, and wide, steady eyes that seem to look straight through the wall.

A tall staff rests in the crook of one arm. Tibetans call him Guru Rinpoche, the precious teacher. Tradition says he came to Tibet from India, met the forces that blocked the teaching, and won them over.
The ancient school of Tibet traces itself back to him. Today: Nyingma.

teach.b: First, the name. Nyingma is usually translated as the ancient ones, or the old school.
It looks back to the early wave of teaching in Tibet, when Indian teachers and Tibetan translators brought the sutras and tantras over the mountains.
Schools that formed later were sometimes called the new ones, and the Nyingma kept the older translations as their own. Second, Padmasambhava, whom you met in year three.
His name is usually rendered lotus-born, and tradition says he appeared as a child sitting in a lotus on a lake.
In the Nyingma story, a Tibetan king invited him, and he helped build the monastery at Samye, taming the spirits of the land so the walls built by day would stop falling down at night.
Whether a listener takes that as history, as teaching, or both, the Nyingma remember him as the one who planted the diamond vehicle in Tibetan ground. Third, Dzogchen.

Nyingma teachers hold up Dzogchen, the great perfection, as the heart of their path: the mind's own nature is already open, clear and awake, and practice is learning to rest in it rather than build it.
Fourth, the shape of the school.
The Nyingma have great monasteries, and also a long line of lay practitioners called ngakpas, who may marry, keep homes, grow their hair long, and still carry the full practice.
The ancient ones were never only behind monastery walls. They lived in villages and on farms too.

how: Nyingma Buddhists honor Padmasambhava, Guru Rinpoche, as the source of their lineage, practice the Dzogchen teachings, and include both monastics and lay yogis called ngakpas.

o: the newest Tibetan school, formed in exile in India
a Tibetan word for the feathered hat of a teacher
the ancient school of Tibet, tracing to Padmasambhava

s: Nyingma practitioners all live in monasteries
the Nyingma also have lay yogis, called ngakpas, who may marry and keep homes.
Tibetans call Padmasambhava Guru Rinpoche, the precious teacher
he's painted on a lotus, with a feathered red hat and a staff.
in Dzogchen, practice means building a pure mind from scratch
Dzogchen teaches resting in the mind's own nature, already open and awake.

games.q: you're Padmasambhava at Samye. every night, the walls built by day fall down. what do you do?
o: give up and go back to India.
tame the spirits of the land so the work can stand.
build the walls twice as fast.
games.why: in the Nyingma story he tamed the spirits of the land, and the monastery could be built.

practice: Picture Padmasambhava in front of you, a little above eye level: the lotus beneath him, the red hat and feather, the steady eyes, the staff in the crook of his arm.
You don't have to believe anything about him to do this; just let the picture be clear and calm. Then let it slowly fade, and rest in whatever is left: open, quiet, awake.

wordCard.voice: Nyingma. The ancient school of Tibetan Buddhism, tracing itself to Padmasambhava and the early translations, with Dzogchen, the great perfection, at its heart. Today's word.

orig.note: Tibetan: nyingma, the old or ancient ones.

carryVoice: Your line: the ancient ones. In monasteries, and in villages too. Until tomorrow.
